chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Whatever there are two of in the body, then for one of them there is half of the diyah, such as the two hands and the two eyes.” I said: If a man’s eye is gouged out? He said: “Half of the diyah.” I said: If a man’s hand is cut off? He said: “In it is half of the diyah.” I said: If one of a man’s testicles is lost? He said: “If it is the left one, then for it there are two-thirds of the diyah.” I said: Why? Did you not say: whatever there are two of in the body, then for one of them there is half of the diyah? He said: “Because the child is from the left testicle.”

key_terms.الْجَسَدِ: the body, in the context of bodily organs subject to legal compensation
key_terms.الْعَيْنَيْنِ: the two eyes, cited as an example of paired organs
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: the two hands, cited as an example of paired organs
key_terms.ثُلُثَا الدِّيَةِ: two-thirds of the prescribed blood-money compensation
key_terms.نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ: half of the prescribed blood-money compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for losing one of a pair of organs according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on diyah for paired bodily organs, stating that the loss of one of two corresponding organs generally entails half of the full diyah. It then presents a specific exception regarding the left testicle, for which two-thirds of the diyah is assigned.
